issues.detail: The Hebrew phrase וּפָנֶיהָ לֹא הָיוּ לָהּ עוֹד (literally 'and her face was no longer [sad] to her') means her countenance was no longer downcast/sad. The Chinese '她的面不再有' ('her face no longer had') is incomplete and omits the implied object (sadness), making it unclear or factually different from the Hebrew meaning.
